summary_paragraph: A woman with type 2 diabetes, neuropathy, gastroparesis, and prior right hallux amputation was admitted for acute left great toe pain and bleeding. She had not yet obtained her custom diabetic shoes. Evaluation revealed exposed bone and soft tissue swelling; imaging showed no acute fracture but chronic changes. She underwent a partial left hallux amputation due to suspected osteomyelitis. Tissue cultures confirmed Staphylococcus aureus infection, and she was treated with IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral antibiotics. Vascular studies showed poor distal foot perfusion consistent with diabetic arterial disease. She developed mild hyponatremia, which improved with supportive care. A small axillary cyst was noted but did not require intervention. She recovered well, with stable diabetes and no signs of systemic infection, and was discharged home with a plan for wound care, six-week antibiotic course, and follow-up with podiatry and primary care.
